title: Tail probability convergence from Gaussian tails
statement: Let $d:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $u:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be sequences, and let $L\in\mathbb R$. If $d(q)\to\infty$ and the standard Gaussian upper tail at $u(q)$ converges to $L$ as $q\to\infty$, then the expected indicator that the normalized Rademacher sum on a uniformly random sign vector of dimension $d(q)$ exceeds $u(q)$ converges to $L$.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ is a sequence of natural numbers
$u$ is a sequence of real numbers
The standard Gaussian upper tail at $u(q)$ converges to $L$
